The Diagram on the Clinic Door

诊室门口的那张示意图 · 649 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A clinic tested a new appointment system. A boy with a painful wrist was sent to a dentist because his previous check involved a tooth. An adult with a chest complaint waited behind him. Her bodily discomfort might be urgent, and her referral recommended immediate assessment. The nurse checked her pulse. Rina paused the trial. A misplaced label could delay diagnosis of an ordinary cramp or a more serious problem. A tidy queue did not establish medical priority.

2Rina followed one patient from the door to the ward. His daughter carried a note describing a neck injury and a possible broken rib. The booking screen kept only the word "checkup." A specialist needed the precise reason for the visit before an examination. The receptionist explained that the system had offered the last entry automatically. It had saved her time on follow-up visits. It had also hidden a correction made after a later diagnosis. Rina drew the steps on paper so the team could see when the information changed.

3A pregnant patient arrived for a preventive checkup before giving birth. Her file mentioned heart surgery, an ear infection, and a recent blood test. A short form mixed current symptoms with an operation she had undergone years earlier. The surgeon's note recommended a specific precaution after tumor treatment. The patient also asked whether an over-the-counter drug could affect the examination. Reception needed to direct the question to a physician, not enroll her in the first clinic named on an old record.

4They redesigned the first screen around today's concern. A bitten lip, a wound on the scalp, and a broken bone could go in one area, with an option to mark severe bleeding. A follow-up after a kidney transplant or other surgical procedure went in another. Cancer treatment needed a different referral from a dental appointment. A nurse could describe an ankle, elbow, or cheek without mistaking it for a diagnosis. A trainee's diligence was still vital when illness could turn fatal.

5A therapist and a psychologist tried the new form. Massage for a calf was different from acute care after a stroke. Fatigue could also be a sign of depression, a digestive disorder, or a reaction to a stimulant. A patient's own words helped a doctor decide whether to diagnose or refer. The team kept a question about recent changes. It applied to someone with an infant at home as much as to a person managing a long recovery.

6Rina asked a nurse to classify three test calls. A stomachache with vomiting needed a different response from a long-standing backache. An itch around a scar might require ordinary advice. A feverish child might not be able to describe the severity. Severe nerve pain or a suspected complication could require a specialist. A treatment plan for a bowel or colon disorder already held useful instructions. Reception could record recommendations and ask a clinician to administer care.

7On the next morning an older man came in after a fall. He had first aid at home, but his forehead hurt and he felt faint. The receptionist recorded that he had already taken a painkiller. A nurse checked his pulse and asked where he had hit his head. The system showed the note to a physician without assigning a diagnosis itself. It also sent an appointment notification to his daughter. She reached the clinic in time to explain a detail the patient had forgotten.

8Rina pinned the diagram beside the door. A junior examiner asked whether they should store a new detail after each visit. Rina drew an arrow for correction and another for deletion. A clinic had to show current concerns even if older cases once seemed more urgent. A grandchild who came with a patient might know what had changed since morning. Staff could ask for that account, then encourage the patient to speak for herself. The blank box had a purpose.

四级汇总词汇 · 13中文译文

诊室门口的那张示意图

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1诊所试用一套新预约系统。一个手腕疼的男孩因为上次查过牙，被分给了牙医。身后一名成人胸口不适，转诊单建议立即评估。护士给她把脉，里娜叫停了试运行。贴错标签，轻则耽误判断抽筋，重则拖延更严重病情。队伍看着整齐，还得看谁真正需要先得到照顾。

2里娜跟着一个病人从门口走到病房。他女儿带来说明，写着颈部受伤、肋骨可能骨折。预约界面却只留“检查”两个字。专科医生检查前需要知道确切的来意。接待员说，系统会自动带出上一次的内容，复诊时省过时间，却也盖住了后来诊断后作出的更正。里娜把流程画在纸上，让大家看信息在哪一步变了。

3一位孕妇来做产前预防性检查。病历提到心脏手术、耳部感染和近期验血。短表把她现在的症状和多年前做过的手术混在一起。外科医生曾注明肿瘤治疗后的一项注意事项。她还想问一种非处方药会不会影响检查。接待员需要把问题转给医生，避免照着旧记录把她排进最先出现的门诊。

4他们围绕当天的问题重做首页。咬伤嘴唇、头皮伤和骨折可以记在一处，并标出是否严重出血。肾移植或其他外科操作后的复查另列。肿瘤治疗所需的转诊也不同于看牙。护士可以说明伤在脚踝、肘部还是脸颊，再由专业人员判断。病情可能危及生命时，新人更需要仔细。

5一位治疗师和一位心理学家试填了表。小腿按摩和中风后的急救显然不同。疲劳可能与抑郁、消化问题或对兴奋剂的反应有关。病人自己怎么说，能帮助医生判断是需要诊断还是转诊。他们留下一个问题，请病人说说最近有什么变化。家里有婴儿的人和正在长期康复的人，都能用上这一项。

6里娜让护士给三通模拟电话分类。肚子疼伴着呕吐，和长期背痛的处理不同。疤痕周围发痒也许只需一般咨询。发烧的孩子未必能描述严重程度。剧烈神经疼或疑似并发症可能需要专科医生。肠道疾病的治疗方案里本来就有有用的指示。接待处可以记录建议，再请医务人员处理。

7第二天，一位老人摔倒后来就诊。他在家先做了急救，可前额疼，还觉得要晕。接待员记下他已吃过止痛药。护士查了脉搏，问头撞在哪里。系统只把记录送给医生，由医生判断，还给女儿发了就诊通知。女儿及时赶到，补上老人忘记的一处细节。

8里娜把示意图贴在门边。一名年轻检查员问，每次看完病是不是都要加一条记录。里娜画了两个箭头，一个用于更正，一个用于删除。旧病例就算曾经更急，眼下的问题也必须看得见。陪同的孙辈也许知道早晨以来发生了什么。工作人员可以先问清，再鼓励病人自己说。表里留一个空白栏，就是为了这一步。
